title: Recursion: Solving a Problem One Smaller Step at a Time
lead: Recursion solves a problem by having a function call itself on a smaller version of the same problem until it reaches a clear stopping point.

sections.heading: The two essential parts
sections.body: Every recursive solution needs a base case that stops the calls and a recursive step that moves toward that base case.

sections.heading: Tracing the calls
sections.body: For factorial(4), think 4 × factorial(3), then 3 × factorial(2), until factorial(1) reaches the base case. The calls then return in reverse order.

tryThis: Trace factorial(4) on paper. Circle the call that reaches the base case and then write the return order.
